The water and spaghetti analogy of procedural games is pretty accurate. It also describes why I find it completely lazy and infuriating for developers to wholly rely upon it.

Procedurally generated content should be complimentary. Not the main focus. The post-beta full-release of Starbound does this rather well, where there are characters and whole areas designed with the intent of being specific challenges (missions, etc), with resource gathering on randomly generated planets as a side mechanic that you have to learn (different planets spawn different mobs that drop different materials, for example).
Just imagine handcrafted story and environment nestled in such procedurally generated universe. That would be so awesome.

And that's where other indies - not funded by big-name studios like Sony or whatever - are stepping in with their procedural sandbox space sims. I've seen several already that support not just ship building, but base building too, among other features.
